nodes.name: MXene synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets with abundant surface functional groups were synthesized by etching and subsequent exfoliation.
nodes.source_text: Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets with abundant surface functional groups were synthesized by etching and subsequent exfoliation.

nodes.name: CoBi/MXene heterostructure formation
nodes.procedure: Co²⁺ ions are readily adsorbed on the surfaces of MXene with abundant negative charge through electrostatic binding. Whereafter, CoBi nanosheets were in situ grown on MXene via chemical reduction triggered by NaBH4 to form CoBi/MXene heterostructures. The formation of the vertically interlaced array structure of CoBi nanoplates standing on MXene sheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM panoramic images show vertically interlaced array structure of CoBi nanoplates standing on MXene sheets (Fig. 2b, S1, S2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of the vertically interlaced array structure of CoBi nanoplates standing on MXene sheets is demonstrated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) panoramic images (Fig. 2b and Fig. S1 and S2, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals ultrathin CoBi nanosheets with well-defined contours and transparent features closely adhering to MXene (Fig. 2c, S3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) examination revealed ultrathin nanosheets with well-defined contours and transparent features. The CoBi nanosheets closely adhere to the MXene (Fig. 2c and Fig. S3, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows overlap of amorphous CoBi and clear lattice fringes of MXene, forming 2D/2D heterostructure (Fig. 2d, S4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image shows the overlap of amorphous CoBi and clear lattice fringes of the MXene nanosheets, resulting in a 2D/2D heterostructure (Fig. 2d and Fig. S4, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: Broad ring SAED pattern reveals amorphous nature of CoBi (inset Fig. 2d).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ambiguous lattice fringes in the HRTEM image and a broad ring selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern for CoBi reveal its amorphous nature...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms amorphous CoBi; weak MXene (002) peak abated in composite due to CoBi coating (Fig. 2e, S5, S6).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ambiguous lattice fringes... confirmed by the XRD pattern (Fig. 2e and Fig. S5, S6, ESI†). The weak MXene diffraction peak can be attributed to the (002) facet...

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of CoBi/MXene is larger than that of CoBi.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area of CoBi/MXene is larger than that of CoBi, endowing it with sufficient active sites...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES of CoBi/MXene shows enhanced whiteline vs CoBi, indicating robust covalent interaction (Fig. 2f).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra of Co K-edge for CoBi/MXene demonstrated an enhanced whiteline intensity compared to CoBi (Fig. 2f)...

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Co–O shell as primary peak followed by Co–Co shell for CoBi/MXene (Fig. 2g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The extended XAFS (EXAFS) analysis (Fig. 2g) revealed that the primary peak was attributed to the single scattering paths of the nearest Co–O shell, followed by a specific Co–Co shell.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p shows Co3+ and Co2+ coexist in both samples; Ti 2p/B 1s confirm Ti–O/Ti–C bonds, no M–B bonds (Fig. S8, Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spin–orbital splitting peaks of Co 2p indicate that Co3+ and Co2+ exist in both CoBi/MXene and CoBi. The fine spectra of Ti 2p and B 1s for CoBi/MXene revealed the coexistence of Ti–O and Ti–C bonds without forming M–B bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XRD shows borates in CoBi/MXene replaced with increasing reduction potential, forming crystalline Co(OH)2 (Fig. 4e).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ XRD patterns revealed that the borates in CoBi/MXene were replaced with increasing reduction potential (Fig. 4e).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of CoBi/MXene shows B–O peak at 680 cm⁻¹ disappearing and Co–OH peak at 496 cm⁻¹ appearing with potential (Fig. 4g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ Raman spectrum of the pristine CoBi/MXene exhibited characteristic peaks of B–O vibration modes at 680 cm⁻¹. As the potential increased, the peak intensity at 496 cm⁻¹ originates from the Co–OH vibration in Co(OH)2.
